claims.text: the hit set holds every reference to create-worktree, worktreeBasePath, WORKTREE_PATH, h2_move, worktree_owner, remove-worktree, worktree-create over the name forms this pass searched

create-worktree name mode overwrites any --parent with <main>/<AFK_WORKTREE_FOLDER, else the provider worktree_folder, else .claude/worktrees> and refuses an absolute or ..-bearing folder with exit 1.

Branch/dir mode takes --parent verbatim, else `afk-config.py resolve worktreeBasePath` run in the main checkout, else ${HOME}/repo-worktrees, and prints the source on stderr; it applies no shape check to --parent or --dir.

A relative --parent is resolved twice: the exists check and mkdir use the caller's cwd, but `git -C "$REPO_DIR" worktree add "$DEST"` resolves it under the main checkout. Probe: `--parent wts` from another folder exited 0, printed the relative `WORKTREE_PATH=wts/d` (the header promises an absolute path, :57), made the worktree at <main>/wts/d and left an empty wts folder in the caller's cwd. AC-051 must refuse this before line 254.
citations: bash tr-A/relparent.sh (temp repo, temp HOME): rc=0, WORKTREE_PATH=wts/d, git worktree list shows probe/main/wts/d

claims.text: Every failure exits 1 with one ERROR= line on stderr through error_exit; the ERR trap under set -eE routes any unexpected failure there; success prints WORKTREE_PATH= as the last stdout line.

A placement helper that fails inside a command substitution trips the ERR trap and exits 1 'unexpected failure near line N' before any exit-3 branch runs; the exit-3 path must test the helper's status explicitly and print ERROR= itself.

All three script callers treat exit 3 as a failure without change: worktree-create.sh passes a non-zero rc through (`${rc/#0/1}`), afk-move.py records the last ERROR= line in the marker, afk-launch.py raises on any non-zero exit with the full stderr; none tests for exit 1 specifically.

run-hook.py returns the WorktreeCreate handler's exit code to Claude Code (hook_failure_notice stderr), so the harness receives 3; a provider with system_message notices would get exit 0 plus a notice document instead.

h2_move.plan predicts <main>/<AFK_WORKTREE_FOLDER or provider worktree_folder or .claude/worktrees>/session-<hex8>, stores {name,path,pane,marker} in <common>/afk-session/<key>.move, and the guard prints that path before the detached afk-move.py runs create-worktree --repo <main> --name <name>, which computes its own DEST.

Moving only one of h2_move.plan and create-worktree name mode to placement makes the refusal's /cd path differ from the created path; both must call one placement function in one commit. test_h2_move.py:67-75 pins the agreement for unlisted repositories only.

plan() never fails by itself: a creation error reaches the guard only through the marker's error key written by afk-move.py, and h2_hint then prints 'the session worktree could not be created'; an exception in plan() becomes the fallback hint. A root refusal can reuse the error key instead of naming a path that is never created (inference).

remove-worktree.py:364 loads h2_move by path for spawn() and catches only OSError and ValueError; the guard imports h2_move under except Exception. h2_move must load the placement module lazily, as owner_env loads worktree_owner, or a load error escapes remove-worktree's session-end waiter (inference).

`placement` already names the guard's place-resolution function (protected_branch_guard.py:209), called as guard.placement by afk-launch.py:31, git-backstop.py:35/66/98 and protected-branch-occupancy.py:24; a module of that name bound at guard module scope would shadow it (inference), so the module or its import alias needs another name.

AFK_WORKTREE_FOLDER (create-worktree:225, h2_move.py:77) and branch/dir --parent are set by the caller's own command, and create-worktree exports AFK_WORKTREE_OP=1 so the git backstop passes its internal git worktree add; the PreToolUse guard sees only the create-worktree call (inference), so for listed repositories both must go through placement's chosen-target check or they bypass AC-053/AC-054.

Name mode appends '/<folder>/' and the plugin runtime paths to <common>/info/exclude; test_create_worktree_name.py:80-89 and :172-183 pin exactly one '/.claude/worktrees/' line. For listed repositories the folder line has no target and should be skipped; the runtime lines still apply (inference).

The lock, the owner record and the copied-file hashes key on the git common dir and on DEST, and the path rewrite derives its target forms from DEST (cygpath), so they follow any parent; PRUNE_PATHS adds the parent only under REPO_DIR and always prunes sibling worktrees.

No test runs branch/dir mode without --parent: every create-worktree-smoke.sh call and the acceptance helper create_worktree() pass --parent, and create-worktree-smoke.sh is not run by CI (tests.yml runs pytest scripts/tests and hooks/tests/hook-smoke.sh; `git grep -n -I -E -e create-worktree-smoke` outside docs/afk finds only CHANGELOG.md, CONFIG.md, hooks/README.md and the script itself).

Creator tests pass the caller's HOME and USERPROFILE (test_create_worktree_name.py:57, test_h2_move.py:29-33), so a placement module reading ~/.afk files reads the developer's real list in them; Windows Python reads USERPROFILE (scripts/tests/test_claude_resolv[e].py:25), so new tests set both, as test_setup_developer_values.py:23 does. The bash fallback ${HOME}/repo-worktrees and a Python '~' can name different folders on Windows (inference).

`afk-config.py resolve` accepts only DEVELOPER_KEYS, the developer child-key table refuses any other developer key, and test_setup_developer_values.py:167 pins developer_values.ORDER == DEVELOPER_KEYS; a `resolve worktreeRoot` (HL-2 sign-off) changes all three in one commit.

Setup H6 offers to drop a machine worktreeBasePath (`worktreeBasePath= --machine`), and AC-043 reads that same value as the legacy root; the offer deletes the migration source unless setup records worktreeRoot first (inference).

/afk:bug resolves K3 worktreeBasePath before calling create-worktree and fails closed only when it does not resolve; for a listed repository the fail-closed case becomes the creator's exit 3, so bug CONFIG.md K3 and dispatch rows and SKILL.md step 5 change, and FRESHNESS.md:79 requires the SKILL.md edit in the same commit (inference).

Same-commit duties: FRESHNESS.md:58 (h2_move placement rule) names SAFETY.md, BEHAVIORS.md, PROVIDERS.md, hooks/README.md, CAPABILITIES.md, six test files and docs/afk/protected-branch-guard/PRD.md; FRESHNESS.md:59 (creator rule) names CONFIG.md, the CAPABILITIES.md events line, both manifests and three test files; MANIFEST.md:1003 describes AFK_WORKTREE_FOLDER; CHANGELOG.md takes a new entry.

A new scripts/ module run under git-bash callers gets a `.gitattributes` eol=lf line by convention (:12-20 list every worktree script); native-contract-gate check I scans only *.sh and hooks/**/*.py, so it would not catch a CRLF scripts/*.py (inference on need; fact on the gate scope).

CONFIG.md:7 and AGENTS.md (CONFIG.md row: 'One reader owns it') forbid a second config parser; placement reading ~/.afk/config.yaml without load() fits only by calling afk-config.py's parse() loaded by path (inference).
CONFIG.md:235 says WorktreeCreated runs after `create-worktree --name`, but create-worktree:508-513 runs it in every mode: the document is narrower than the code.

Proposed verdict for seams (a) and (b): extends. The output contract (last stdout WORKTREE_PATH=, ERROR= on stderr, exit 1) and every caller's parsing survive; additions are exit 3, a placement branch in both modes, a chosen-target check for --parent and AFK_WORKTREE_FOLDER, and h2_move.plan calling the same function. Dependent behaviour changes: listed repositories leave <main>/.claude/worktrees (pinned for unlisted repos by test_create_worktree_name.py:76, test_h2_move.py:73, test_protected_branch_acceptance.py:877); branch/dir mode stops using worktreeBasePath for them (bug K3, setup H6); the env and flag overrides stop placing them; no exclude folder line is written for them.

Today an agent's `git worktree add` is no identified mutation: the operations list records only worktree move/remove and git_mutates is true for worktree only on move/remove, so decide() allows it at the no-resource return.

The add refusal must enter as a new `worktree-add` operation, never as a git_mutates verb: git_mutates feeds the folder-resource loop, which refuses any main-checkout mutation whatever the repository, so unlisted adds from the main checkout would be refused against AC-055.

The existing operations loop refuses an operand whose placement is None ('could not be resolved'); an add target does not exist yet, so add needs its own branch ahead of worktree_target, else every add is refused.

_git_positionals skips option words but not their values: `git worktree add -b feat ../x main` gives operands [feat, ../x, main] and `--reason why --lock ../x` gives [why, ../x]; the add parser must consume -b, -B and --reason values.

Target parsing today: quotes make a path with spaces one word, `git -C <dir>` moves the folder relative operands resolve against, `~` expands with the hook's HOME, and resolve() uses abspath/normpath with no realpath, so a symlink or junction is not followed; realpath of a missing path cost 0.39 ms median in the lab.

`git worktree move <wt> <existing dir>` lands at `<existing dir>/<basename>` (lab), while the guard judges the literal destination operand; the root check must append the basename when the destination exists.

The session repository is found by placement(cwd) from the file layout (.git directory, or gitdir file plus commondir) with git rev-parse only for unusual layouts; a linked worktree's main checkout is common.parent when the common dir is named .git, the rule h2_move.plan already uses.

Per call the guard reads every providers/*.json, runs the lavish rule, the session placement and the change-meter hold; it imports no afk-config.py and reads no ~/.afk file on a call with no identified mutation; the protection lookup reads ~/.afk/config.yaml and calls afk-config load() only when a branch verdict is computed.

The other PreToolUse handler, run-hook.py repo-list, already spawns git and loads afk-config.py with load(root) on each call it does not bail, and same-event handlers run in parallel, so the event's wall time is its slowest handler.

Measured baseline: the guard deciding a `git worktree add ../x` Bash call (allowed) took median 437 ms from the main checkout and 429 ms from a linked worktree (n=15 each, 1 warm-up); interpreter start alone 146 ms; the bench has no guard budget.

Measured placement read in a fresh guard process: afk-config.py loaded by path 1.27 ms median with warm bytecode (12.1 ms without a bytecode cache), a 10-line machine file parse 0.38 ms, a 3-entry repositories.json load 0.21 ms; total 1.85 ms median (max 9.2 ms) warm and 12.8 ms median (max 56.6 ms) cold, n=21; repeated in one process (n=25) import 0.50 ms, parse 0.23 ms, list 0.15 ms; load(None) 128 ms, load(root) 0.27 ms.

claims.text: The guard's shell parser records a worktree operation only for `move` and `remove`, and git_mutates counts only those as worktree mutations; an agent's `git worktree add` yields no operation and no resource, so the guard never sees it today. _git_positionals skips option words but keeps their values, so `git worktree add -b <branch> <path>` gives <branch> as the first operand; an add parser built on it must consume the values of -b, -B and --reason.

shell_mutations.resolve expands `~` and normalises with abspath or normpath but never follows a symlink or junction, so it does not give the design's real target; remove-worktree.py inside() already compares realpath + normcase prefixes.

worktree_target resolves a move/remove target through registered worktrees, and the loop checks a move destination only when placement() finds a checkout there; an add target and a fresh move destination are paths placement() returns None for, so the root rule needs its own check on the resolved operand.

The guard module already defines placement() (the checkout kind of a path), called by decide, worktree_target and hooks/git-backstop.py; a shared module named placement collides with that name inside the guard (inferred naming hazard).

refusal() always appends the AFK_ALLOW_PROTECTED=1 human launch sentence, main() returns 0 before decide() when that flag is set, and hooks/git-backstop.py:29 is a second caller of refusal(); a placement refusal through decide() is therefore lifted by the human flag, and a signature change reaches the backstop.

decide() allows any call whose mutation parse raises, so an exception in a new add parse or in a placement read made inside mutation_targets fails open; a fault after the mutation is identified fails closed inside a work tree.

create-worktree's only error path, error_exit, hard-codes exit 1 and the ERR trap routes every unexpected failure to it; a new exit 3 needs a second exit path that still writes ERROR= as the last line, and the name-mode refusal of a folder outside the main checkout (exit 1) is the opposite of the listed-repository rule.
